advice: Experiment: in the n=512 generated-reference path, test padding only the per-call FP32 scratch panel stride from 512 floats to 544 floats (512 data floats plus 32 padding floats per row). Update every scratch-panel address calculation and allocation size together; keep the logical 512-element row contents, FP32 arithmetic, kernel tiling, and ABI unchanged. This changes the row byte stride from 2048 to 2176, which may reduce repeated cache-set conflicts for the packed scratch accesses on the 128-byte-line M4 Pro caches. The hypothesis is falsifiable: compare the padded version with the unchanged source using the fixed benchmark and unchanged paired controls, while including the larger allocation and all packing traffic inside gemm. Check scratch accesses stay within the enlarged allocation, logical rows do not overlap, outputs meet the 0.002 tolerance, and general-size/tail handling is unchanged. Treat any score difference as unverified until repeated measurements exceed observed noise.
risks: The actual cache-set mapping is not supplied, so the proposed stride may not reduce conflicts; it may instead increase cache and TLB pressure or packing cost. The n=512 generated path shown uses a 512-float scratch stride in its explicit offsets, so a padding experiment requires a consistent rewrite of those offsets and allocation, and could introduce address or bounds errors. No performance result can be inferred from the evidence provided.
